results.title: SeGPruner: Semantic-Geometric Visual Token Pruner for 3D Question Answering
results.abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) have been widely adopted for 3D question answering (3D QA). In typical pipelines, visual tokens extracted from multiple viewpoints are concatenated with language tokens and jointly processed by a large language model (LLM) for inference. However, aggregating multi-view observations inevitably introduces severe token redundancy, leading to an overly large visual token set that significantly hinders inference efficiency under constrained token budgets. Visual token pruning has emerged as a prevalent strategy to address this issue. Nevertheless, most existing pruners are primarily tailored to 2D inputs or rely on indirect geometric cues, which limits their ability to explicitly retain semantically critical objects and maintain sufficient spatial coverage for robust 3D reasoning. In this paper, we propose SeGPruner, a semantic-aware and geometry-guided token reduction framework for efficient 3D QA with multi-view images. Specifically, SeGPruner first preserves semantically salient tokens through an attention-based importance module (Saliency-aware Token Selector), ensuring that object-critical evidence is retained. It then complements these tokens with spatially diverse ones via a geometry-guided selector (Geometry-aware Token Diversifier), which jointly considers semantic relevance and 3D geometric distance. This cooperation between saliency preservation and geometry-guided diversification balances object-level evidence and global scene coverage under aggressive token reduction. Extensive experiments on ScanQA and OpenEQA demonstrate that SeGPruner substantially improves inference efficiency, reducing the visual token budget by 91% and inference latency by 86%, while maintaining competitive performance in 3D reasoning tasks.

results.title: The Model in the Middle: Toward AI-Native Real-Time Communication
results.abstract: Full-duplex omni models are transforming human--AI interaction from turn-based exchanges into continuous multimodal conversations in which speaking, listening, and reasoning unfold concurrently. Rather than viewing the model as a replacement for a human endpoint, we argue for a new perspective: the model is a stateful computational middlebox inside a human-centered feedback loop, with network transport, model serving, and user playback jointly shaping how the interaction evolves. This perspective breaks the traditional boundaries among stages designed around local objectives. Rather than optimizing them in isolation, an AI-native real-time stack should allow the state of each stage to shape the actions of the others. We explore three cross-stage coordination opportunities: network-aware inference scheduling, execution-aware transport prioritization, and playback control that accounts for both network and model variability. We are building Conflux to explore these ideas, and preliminary results show substantial improvements in response latency and playback deadline adherence under network degradation. More broadly, we call for an AI-native real-time communication stack that resolve the joint control problem spanning communication, computation, and playback.

results.title: PRESAGE: Uncertainty-Aware Predictive Elastic Scheduling for Cloud Analytics and GenAI Inference
results.abstract: Cloud data platforms increasingly co-locate hybrid analytical workloads (data-lake/warehouse queries, batch and stream engines) with generative-AI (GenAI) inference services, producing load traces that are strongly bursty, heavy-tailed, and multi-phase. Reactive threshold autoscalers and simple ARIMA/LSTM predictors react poorly to such dynamics, causing service-level-objective (SLO) violations or resource waste. Time-series foundation models (TSFMs) offer strong zero-shot forecasting, but they are not adapted to multivariate, non-stationary cloud load, and, critically, forecasting is usually decoupled from scheduling, so predictive uncertainty never reaches the decision. We present Presage, an end-to-end framework that closes this loop. Presage 1) domain-adapts a pretrained TSFM to multivariate cloud traces through parameter-efficient fine-tuning and continual pretraining with a lightweight cross-channel adapter, enabling few-shot cross-cluster transfer; 2) introduces retrieval-augmented time-series forecasting, conditioning the predictor on the most similar historical windows drawn from a pattern library to capture periodic events and recurring spikes; 3) propagates calibrated probabilistic forecasts (conformalized quantiles) into an uncertainty-aware reinforcement-learning scheduler that chooses a per-service risk level under an explicit cost–SLO constraint, with dedicated prefill/decode provisioning for GenAI; and 4) jointly performs load forecasting and anomaly-precursor detection for robustness. We instantiate Presage on a publicly available TimesFM-1.0-200M backbone and evaluate it on six public traces from Alibaba (a GenAI Stable-Diffusion serving trace), Microsoft Azure (two LLM-inference traces, serverless functions, and VMs), and Google Borg, using a trace-driven simulator, a real vLLM serving harness, and a small 8-GPU Kubernetes testbed. In this evaluation Presage reduces forecast CRPS by up to 28% over the best zero-shot TSFM while attaining near-nominal coverage at every quantile the scheduler consumes, and cuts SLO violations by 3– $5\times $ at $\sim \!18\%$ lower resource cost than strong predictive and RL baselines, with KV-cache out-of-memory events reduced from 27 to 1 for GenAI serving; an adaptive online conformal variant further improves worst-window coverage under drift. Because the coverage guarantees we inherit are marginal and hold only under approximate exchangeability, and because the testbed is small-scale, we state the resulting scope limits explicitly. The code will be released publicly upon acceptance.
